executive_summary: An archived one-time backfill script (scripts/archive/one-time/backfill-prd-integration.js) wrote fabricated boilerplate prose into product_requirements_v2.integration_operationalization for 707 rows before an offset-pagination-over-a-shrinking-predicate bug silently stalled it. These 707 rows are indistinguishable from genuine content at a glance and score 100%/complete on GATE_INTEGRATION_SECTION_VALIDATION despite carrying no real per-PRD content -- identified via the exact predicate integration_operationalization->consumers->0->>name = 'LEO Protocol Engine' (verified live: exactly 707 rows, 15 distinct fabricated jsonb variants sharing one 5-key keyset). This SD replaces those 707 rows' integration_operationalization with the same honest null-per-key placeholder shape (buildDefaultIntegrationOperationalization(), scripts/prd/prd-creator.js:608) already used by the sibling SD-LEARN-FIX-ADDRESS-PAT-LES-012 backfill, which is proven gate-verdict-identical to NULL across every sd_type by the existing tests/unit/gates/integration-section-parity.test.js suite. LEAD-phase Explore + VALIDATION sub-agent review refuted the SD's originally-stated write mechanism: integration_operationalization is its own top-level jsonb column (confirmed via information_schema.columns), separate from metadata, so the generalized mergeJsonbColumn/JSONB_MERGE_ALLOWLIST infrastructure (jsonbColumn:'metadata' hardcoded for this table) cannot target it -- and even if it could, mergeJsonbColumn performs a `||` MERGE not a REPLACE, and has no CAS/extra-guard capability, both of which this SD's safety story requires. The corrected mechanism is a direct guarded UPDATE (supabase-js seam) modeled on the precedented sibling script scripts/one-off/backfill-integration-operationalization-v2.mjs, using its updated_at CAS-guard pattern.

functional_requirements.title: Replace the 707 fabricated integration_operationalization rows with the honest null-per-key placeholder
functional_requirements.description: Write a one-off backfill script (modeled on scripts/one-off/backfill-integration-operationalization-v2.mjs) that identifies target rows LIVE at execution time via integration_operationalization->consumers->0->>name = 'LEO Protocol Engine' (not a hardcoded 707 count -- VALIDATION measured a 706-vs-707 historical drift in the archived script's own commit message vs. live state), and for each matching row performs a direct guarded UPDATE via supabase-js setting integration_operationalization = buildDefaultIntegrationOperationalization() (imported from scripts/prd/prd-creator.js). The write must NOT use mergeJsonbColumn (confirmed wrong tool: separate top-level column, merge-not-replace semantics, no CAS capability -- see LEAD-phase correction in this SD's description). Use keyset pagination over id (not offset, to avoid repeating the archived script's exact defect class), batch size ~100-500.
acceptance_criteria: Target rows are enumerated via a live query against the fabrication predicate at execution time, not a hardcoded row count or id list

Each UPDATE sets integration_operationalization to exactly buildDefaultIntegrationOperationalization()'s output (5 canonical keys, each null) -- imported from scripts/prd/prd-creator.js, not reimplemented

Each UPDATE is guarded by a compare-and-swap on updated_at read immediately before the write (matching backfill-integration-operationalization-v2.mjs's writeBackfillRow pattern), so a row that changed between read and write is skipped, not clobbered

updated_by is set on every UPDATE to a script/SD-identifying value (never 'EXEC', per enforce_doctrine_of_constraint) -- an improvement over the sibling script, which left it null and got changed_by='SYSTEM' in the audit trail
Keyset (not offset) pagination is used to enumerate rows in batches
After the script runs to completion, zero rows remain matching the fabrication predicate live

functional_requirements.title: Prove gate-verdict parity is preserved (no false-positive/false-negative shift)
functional_requirements.description: The existing tests/unit/gates/integration-section-parity.test.js suite (from the sibling SD) already proves buildDefaultIntegrationOperationalization()'s output scores byte-identical to NULL on GATE_INTEGRATION_SECTION_VALIDATION across every sd_type -- this SD does not need to re-derive that proof, but must run the suite as part of its own verification (not merely cite it) to confirm it still passes unmodified after this SD's changes (this SD makes no code change to the gate or the placeholder builder, only to data).
acceptance_criteria: tests/unit/gates/integration-section-parity.test.js passes unmodified after this SD's changes
A live spot-check of 5+ corrected rows confirms GATE_INTEGRATION_SECTION_VALIDATION's validator scores them identically to how it would score a NULL integration_operationalization value

functional_requirements.title: Regression/verification coverage for the backfill script itself
functional_requirements.description: Add tests (or a documented dry-run + live-verification procedure, consistent with how the sibling backfill-integration-operationalization-v2.mjs was verified) proving: the fabrication predicate correctly selects only the 707 (or live-drifted count of) contaminated rows and none of the genuine/v2-placeholder rows; the CAS guard correctly skips a row that changed since being read; the script is idempotent (a second run against already-corrected rows is a no-op, since they no longer match the fabrication predicate).
acceptance_criteria: A unit or integration-style test (against a fixture or a narrowly-scoped live check) proves the fabrication predicate does not match any of the 1,570 pre-existing v2-placeholder rows or the ~2,568 genuine rows
A test or documented manual verification proves the updated_at CAS guard causes a stale-read row to be skipped rather than overwritten
Running the script a second time after a successful first run performs zero writes (idempotency), verified by re-running it against a state where the fabrication predicate no longer matches

functional_requirements.title: Archive-script hardening follow-up (in scope per SD text)
functional_requirements.description: Guard scripts/archive/one-time/backfill-prd-integration.js so it cannot be accidentally re-run and reproduce the same class of defect -- e.g. a top-of-file guard that exits immediately with an explanatory message (referencing this SD and the corrected sibling script), or deletion if the archived script serves no historical-reference purpose. EXEC's choice between guard-in-place vs. delete, but the decision and rationale must be documented in the PR.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/archive/one-time/backfill-prd-integration.js either refuses to execute (with a clear message pointing to this SD and the corrected approach) or is removed, with the choice documented in the PR description
If guarded rather than removed, a smoke-test confirms invoking the script exits non-zero without performing any writes

technical_requirements.title: No schema change
technical_requirements.description: This is a code + data-correction fix. No migration, no new table/column. integration_operationalization and metadata remain the existing separate top-level jsonb columns on product_requirements_v2.

technical_requirements.title: supabase-js write seam only
technical_requirements.description: The write path must use supabase-js, not a raw-pg client. updated_at is a `timestamp WITHOUT time zone` column; VALIDATION confirmed the node pg driver shifts naive timestamps by machine offset, which would silently break the updated_at CAS guard on a raw-pg seam (every UPDATE matching 0 rows). supabase-js was verified (read-only round-trip) to compare updated_at correctly.

technical_requirements.title: Do not extend JSONB_MERGE_ALLOWLIST/mergeJsonbColumn for this SD
technical_requirements.description: VALIDATION assessed and rejected extending the shared lib/coordinator/safe-metadata-merge.mjs primitive to support a second jsonb column per table: it would require four separate changes (jsonbColumn scalar->array, new extraGuardColumns entry, a new guard mechanism that doesn't exist today, a new replace-vs-merge mode) driven by a single one-off, and mergeJsonbColumn has zero production callers against product_requirements_v2 today. The precedented, already-fit-for-purpose sibling script is the correct model instead.

technical_requirements.title: DB triggers are live constraints, not defects to route around
technical_requirements.description: trg_validate_integration_section_keys (BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE) hard-rejects any integration_operationalization key outside the canonical 5 -- buildDefaultIntegrationOperationalization()'s output is compliant; no provenance marker may be embedded inside this column (use metadata instead, if a provenance stamp is desired). enforce_doctrine_of_constraint (BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE, SECURITY DEFINER) hard-aborts if COALESCE(created_by, updated_by) = 'EXEC' -- never set updated_by to that value.

risks.risk: RULED OUT DURING LEAD (recorded for history, not a live risk): the SD originally proposed mergeJsonbColumn/JSONB_MERGE_ALLOWLIST as the write mechanism. Explore + VALIDATION sub-agent review confirmed integration_operationalization is a separate top-level jsonb column from metadata, that the allowlist entry hardcodes jsonbColumn:'metadata', and that mergeJsonbColumn performs a merge (not replace) with no CAS capability -- wrong tool regardless of the allowlist. Corrected to a direct guarded UPDATE modeled on the precedented sibling script before PLAN began.
risks.mitigation: N/A -- design was corrected in LEAD before PLAN/EXEC; FR-1 now specifies the data-supported mechanism directly.

risks.risk: The 707 rows contain 15 distinct fabricated jsonb variants (not 1), all sharing the same 5-key keyset but differing in value -- a naive idempotency/verification check that assumes a single expected old blob would be wrong.
risks.mitigation: FR-1/FR-3 require keying verification on the consumers[0].name predicate, never an expected old blob.

risks.risk: A raw-pg write seam would silently break the updated_at CAS guard due to the node pg driver's naive-timestamp machine-offset shift, causing every UPDATE to match 0 rows and the script to falsely report zero progress.
risks.mitigation: TR-2 mandates the supabase-js seam, verified via a read-only CAS round-trip test (positive/negative control) during LEAD-phase VALIDATION.

risks.risk: A bulk 707-row UPDATE adds meaningfully to governance_audit_log (measured ~29MB against a 5.5GB table, ~0.5% growth).
risks.mitigation: Acceptable and desirable -- this is the same mechanism that enabled full rollback of the sibling SD's earlier destroyed-keys incident; not a reason to avoid triggering it.
